lecture_summary: Develops two-source interference from sinusoidal-wave phase: converting path difference and initial source phase into phase difference, classifying constructive/destructive interference, and solving geometric sound/radio examples while checking allowed interference orders.

videos.title: Mechanical Waves Physics Practice Problems - Basic Introduction
videos.reason: Builds the needed foundation in wave graphs, wavelength, frequency, and wave speed, supporting v=fλ and the lecture’s wavefront interpretations.

videos.title: Young's Double Slit Experiment
videos.reason: The playlist’s strongest direct treatment of coherent two-source constructive/destructive interference, path geometry, and interference order; the principles transfer from light to the lecture’s sound and radio sources.

coverage_gaps: No strong match explicitly develops traveling-wave phase, k=2π/λ, or spatial phase difference Δφ=2πΔx/λ.
No playlist entry directly covers Δφ=2πΔr/λ+Δφ₀, particularly the crucial contribution from initially out-of-phase sources.
The radio-antenna, flute, and speaker-position examples—computing exact path lengths, reducing phase modulo 2π, retaining m, and testing geometrically allowed orders—have no strong match.
Partial interference and the distinction between an interference location and a permanently fixed crest or trough are not clearly covered.
